Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Difficulty breathing after insect sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient was stung by a bee or wasp a few minutes prior to presentation.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Stung by a bee/wasp a few minutes prior

History_of_Present_Illness.content: There is a puncture mark on the right arm with localized erythematous rash after the sting.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: puncture mark on right arm with localized erythematous rash

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports mild breathing difficulty after the insect sting.
Patient reports that his tongue feels a bit weird after the sting.
Patient reports possible lip swelling after the sting.
Onset of symptoms was minutes ago.
Patient has never had an EpiPen.
Patient reports no known pet allergies.
Patient reports no known food allergies.
Patient has not taken an antihistamine yet for this episode.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has occasional anxiety or panic symptoms and is not on medication for them.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Other: occasional anxiety/panic symptoms, not on meds

Medications.content: No medications were reported taken for this episode.
Medications.source_text: Meds: none reported taken for this episode

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a computer scientist.

Assessment.content: Localized allergic or inflammatory reaction to insect sting with right arm erythema and puncture, without systemic or anaphylactic features observed.
Assessment.source_text: 1. Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to insect sting — right arm erythema and puncture; no systemic/anaphylactic features observed

Assessment.content: Reported mild respiratory symptoms and anxiety with subjective throat and tongue sensation and concern for lip swelling, but no objective airway compromise.
Assessment.source_text: 2. Reported mild respiratory symptoms/anxiety — subjective throat/tongue sensation and concern for lip swelling, but no objective airway compromise

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised over-the-counter chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg orally up to every 6 hours as needed.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Antihistamine: advised OTC chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg PO — up to q6h as needed

Plan_of_Care.content: Once-daily non-sedating antihistamine is an acceptable alternative and can be purchased over the counter.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: OR once-daily non-sedating antihistamine acceptable; can be purchased over the counter

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to go to A&E urgently if new or worsening lip or tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, stridor, hypotension, or rapid symptom progression occur.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety-netting: advised to go to A&E urgently if any progression — new/worsening lip or tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, stridor, hypotension, or rapid symptom progression

Plan_of_Care.content: If redness spreads, becomes hot, or there are signs of local infection, patient should consider GP review and antibiotic assessment.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: If redness spreads, becomes hot, or signs of local infection → consider GP review/antibiotic assessment

Plan_of_Care.content: No immediate need for EpiPen or allergy testing; review or refer if recurrent reactions.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: No immediate need for EpiPen or allergy testing now; review/refer if recurrent reactions

Plan_of_Care.content: Provided reassurance and advised a low threshold to re-contact the service if concerned or if symptoms change.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Reassurance and low threshold to re-contact service if concerned or symptoms change

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient was advised to go to A&E urgently if symptoms progress, including new or worsening lip or tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, stridor, hypotension, or rapid symptom progression.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Safety-netting: advised to go to A&E urgently if any progression — new/worsening lip or tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, stridor, hypotension, or rapid symptom progression

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient was advised to seek GP review or antibiotic assessment if redness spreads, becomes hot, or there are signs of local infection.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: If redness spreads, becomes hot, or signs of local infection → consider GP review/antibiotic assessment

Follow_up_Information.content: Future review or referral is planned if recurrent reactions occur.
Patient was advised to re-contact the service if concerned or if symptoms change.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Reassurance and low threshold to re-contact service if concerned or symptoms change

Physical_Findings.content: Patient is talking normally and breathing appears unlabored to the clinician.
Physical_Findings.source_text: General: talking normally; breathing appears unlabored to clinician

Physical_Findings.content: On oral and throat inspection while the patient said "ah," there was no visible oral or pharyngeal mucosal swelling.
Physical_Findings.source_text: HEENT/oral airway: oral/throat inspected (patient said "ah") — no visible oral or pharyngeal mucosal swelling

Physical_Findings.content: Lips were not visibly swollen on examination.
Right arm shows a puncture mark with slight redness and a blotchy rash.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Skin: right arm puncture mark with slight redness/blotchy rash

Physical_Findings.content: No marked local swelling or warmth was noted at the right arm puncture site.
Physical_Findings.source_text: no marked local swelling or warmth noted

Physical_Findings.content: No stridor or respiratory distress was observed.
Physical_Findings.source_text: No stridor or respiratory distress observed
